_note: ILLUSTRATIVE placeholder answers of Anord Mardix for RC-1 (OPP-0003), written for the PoC demo (P-49 part B). Not real unit positions; no rating, certification or figure here is a verified fact.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our prefabricated power pods and skids are laid out for concurrent maintenance and the block-plus-catcher arrangement, and are designed for 35 °C ambient with 38 to 40 °C peaks and outdoor use from -30 to 40 °C with stated derating. The C5 corrosion class and 120 mph wind rating need an upgraded outdoor enclosure that we would confirm in design.
answers.reason: C5 corrosion protection and the 120 mph wind rating are not in the standard pod enclosure; they need an engineered enclosure option. The 45 °C facility water point (DB-08) is the cooling team's scope.
answers.conditions: Seismic category D anchoring to be confirmed against the Owner's site data.
answers.next_steps: Confirm the enclosure option and its effect on price and lead time before the final tender.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We would supply the 800 VDC two-wire chain for Lot 3: DC switchboards at the power-block output, 6000 A-class busduct and parallel 1250 A row busways with 125 A tap cans, as one coordinated design.
answers.conditions: DC ratings of the busway and tap cans to be confirmed by type testing during detailed design.
answers.next_steps: Share the single-line diagram for Lot 3 at the first dialogue session.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our Lot 3 switchboards and busway would be designed to IEC 60664-1 clearance and creepage for overvoltage category III in the power room and II in the data room, with pollution degree 2 or 3 by zone, and protection on both ungrounded poles. Each separately derived system would carry its grounding compatibility on the nameplate.
answers.reason: Isolation where MV AC connects to the 800 VDC system sits in the power blocks (MV AC to 800 VDC conversion), which are not offered in this tender (capability gap REQ-0003-0213); our answer covers the 800 VDC distribution side.
answers.conditions: We coordinate isolation and grounding with the power-block supplier at the Lot 2 to Lot 3 interface.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our power monitoring and DCIM would integrate every Lot 3 signal with the Owner's electrical power management system over open protocols. We would provide Modbus TCP and SNMP natively and Redfish through a protocol gateway rather than on each device.
answers.reason: Redfish is not native on our switchboard and busway monitoring devices today.
answers.workaround: Modbus TCP and SNMP from each device, with a redundant gateway publishing the same points over Redfish to the Owner's system.
answers.next_steps: Agree the point list and gateway arrangement with the Owner's controls consultant.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our circuit monitoring would measure power, voltage and energy at every row busway and tap can, with sampling rate, accuracy and timestamps stated in the technical tender. Energy per node and per user job comes from the compute system, which can take our circuit data as an input.
answers.reason: Per-node and per-job energy is measured inside the compute rack, outside our equipment; we cover the power distribution level only.
answers.next_steps: Align the data exchange with the compute team so job energy can be reconciled with circuit readings.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our Lot 3 equipment would be rated and protected to ride through the disturbances foreseeable within the Section 9 interface limits, including the stated ripple and regulation on the 800 VDC input.
answers.next_steps: List the design margins against each Section 9 limit in the technical tender.

Illustrative placeholder response: We would provide five years of maintenance and support from acceptance, 24 by 7 with a four-hour response and concurrent maintenance, through our field service team and on-site spares. We propose a longer repair time for non-cabinet items than the 2 hours requested.
answers.reason: A 2-hour repair on power distribution equipment is not realistic without a resident engineer on site.
answers.workaround: Repair within 8 hours for non-cabinet items using the on-site spares; a resident engineer to meet 2 hours is offered as a priced option.
answers.next_steps: Discuss the repair targets in the dialogue sessions.

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: We accept liquidated damages for missed service levels, capped by the at-risk amounts described, and delay penalties that scale with the length of the delay and the seriousness of the breach, subject to an aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together.
answers.reason: Liquidated damages and delay penalties have no overall limit as written, which leaves an open-ended risk on a phased multi-lot delivery.
answers.workaround: An aggregate cap on liquidated damages and delay penalties together, set as a percentage of each lot's price; the percentage is stated in the financial offer and listed in the commercial exceptions schedule (CT-08).

answers.response: Illustrative placeholder response: Our commercial exceptions are listed in the separate exceptions schedule and kept to a minimum: on liquidated damages, only the aggregate cap per lot asked for under CT-07; any indexed price is shown there only as an alternative to the firm price.

Illustrative placeholder response: Warranty on our Lot 3 equipment would run within the five-year maintenance period, and we accept responsibility for failures caused by disturbances that are foreseeable within the Section 9 interface limits.

Illustrative placeholder response: We provide a supply-chain security and risk plan for our Lot 3 equipment, with mitigation for sensitive components such as protection relays and monitoring electronics. Instead of a guarantee for each original component over the system's whole lifetime, we commit to the availability period stated as the proposed change.
answers.reason: No supplier can guarantee every original component for an open-ended system lifetime: electronic parts follow their makers' life cycles.
answers.workaround: Spare parts or compatible form-fit-function replacements available for at least 10 years from acceptance, with at least 12 months' notice of end of life and a last-time-buy offer before any component is discontinued.
